q: How far before scheduled departure must a pilot check in for the originating flight of a pairing?
a: One hour prior, or 45 minutes for deadheading.

src.quote: Pilots shall check in one hour prior (45 minutes for deadheading) to the scheduled departure of the originating flight of a pairing.
src.note: Missing the one-hour check-in can trigger assignment of a reserve pilot and a possible 'No Show' pending Base Chief Pilot review.

q: A pilot may voluntarily check in earlier than one hour before departure, but no earlier than what limit?
a: No earlier than four hours prior to the scheduled departure.

src.quote: a pilot may voluntarily check-in prior to one hour, but in no case earlier than four hours prior to the scheduled departure.
src.note: Early check-in is at the individual pilot's discretion but is bounded at four hours before scheduled departure.

q: What is the minimum pilot crew for a flight, and how are the two positions designated?
a: Two pilots: one designated as Pilot-In-Command and one as Second-In-Command.

src.quote: The minimum pilot crew is two pilots; one pilot designated as Pilot-In-Command and one as Second-In-Command.
src.note: Each pilot is designated no more than one Flight Crew function per flight segment.

q: Under Part 117 Table A (unaugmented), what maximum flight time applies for a report time of 0500-1959 versus 0000-0459 or 2000-2359?
a: 9 hours for a report time of 0500-1959; 8 hours for report times of 0000-0459 or 2000-2359.

src.quote: the flight time limits in Table A of Part 117 (unaugmented operations) restrict a Flight Crewmember’s time on task (flight time) to either 8 or 9 hours.
src.note: Table A is entered using the report time at local domicile or the acclimated local time in theater; 0500-1959 gives 9 hours, the two night bands give 8.

q: For augmented operations, the Part 117 flight time limits restrict time on task to what values for a 3-pilot crew versus a 4-pilot crew?
a: 13 hours for a 3-pilot crew and 17 hours for a 4-pilot crew.

src.quote: Flight time limits (augmented operations) restrict a Flight Crewmember’s time on task (flight time) to either 13 hours (3-pilot crew) or 17 hours (4-pilot crew).
src.note: These are flight-time (time-on-task) limits, distinct from the Flight Duty Period limits in Tables B and C.

q: What are the cumulative flight time limitations a Flight Crewmember may not exceed under Part 117?
a: 100 hours in any 672 consecutive hours, or 1000 hours in any 365 consecutive calendar-day period.

src.quote: A Flight Crewmember’s cumulative FTL shall not exceed: • 100 hours in any 672 consecutive hours, or • 1000 hours in any 365 consecutive calendar-day period.
src.note: Cumulative FTL uses rolling windows of 672 consecutive hours and 365 consecutive calendar days and includes all Part 91 and 121 flying.

q: What are the cumulative Flight Duty Period (FDP) limits under Part 117?
a: 60 FDP hours in any 168 consecutive hours, or 190 FDP hours in any 672 consecutive hours.

src.quote: • 60 FDP hours in any 168 consecutive hours, or • 190 FDP hours in any 672 consecutive hours.
src.note: A post-takeoff FDP extension may exceed these cumulative limits only to the extent necessary to complete the flight; it expires once the aircraft lands.

q: What is the minimum rest period Part 117 prescribes before a RAP or between FDPs, and what sleep opportunity must it provide?
a: 10 consecutive hours measured from release from duty, providing a minimum of 8 uninterrupted hours of sleep opportunity.

src.quote: the minimum rest period (prior to beginning a Reserve Availability Period (RAP) or between FDPs) as 10 consecutive hours measured from the time the Flight Crewmember is released from duty. This 10-hour rest period must provide the Flight Crewmember with a minimum of 8 uninterrupted hours of sleep opportunity.
src.note: If the pilot determines the rest will not provide 10 hours or the 8 uninterrupted sleep hours, they must notify Pilot Crew Scheduling.

q: What is the maximum FDP extension permitted under 14 CFR 117.19?
a: Up to 2 hours; no prior extension over 30 minutes since the last 30 consecutive hours free from duty.

src.quote: Flight Duty Period (FDP) extensions of up to 2 hours are permitted provided:
src.note: Other conditions: the extension addresses unforeseen operational circumstances, CBA/PWA limits are not exceeded, and the PIC and certificate holder agree on the length.

q: How does a Flight Crewmember become acclimated to a new theater under Part 117?
a: 36 consecutive hours of rest in the new theater, or 72 hours in the new theater.

src.quote: A Flight Crewmember operating in a new theater that has received 36 consecutive hours of rest, or who has been in a new theater for 72 hours, is considered to be acclimated to that new theater.
src.note: If a crewmember transitions theaters and is not acclimated, the Table B or Table C maximum FDP limit must be reduced by 30 minutes.

q: How does Part 117 define a 'theater' for acclimation purposes?
a: A geographical area where the FDP departure and arrival points differ by no more than 60 degrees of longitude.

src.quote: Theater means a geographical area in which the distance between the Flight Crewmember’s flight duty period departure point and arrival point differs by no more than 60 degrees of longitude.
src.note: The same 60-degree-longitude threshold drives theater-change compensatory rest in 4.3.2.11.

q: What is the minimum recline requirement that defines a Class 3 rest facility?
a: A cabin or Flight Deck seat reclining at least 40 degrees with leg and foot support.

src.quote: Class 3 rest facility means a seat in an aircraft cabin or Flight Deck that reclines at least 40 degrees and provides leg and foot support.
src.note: Class 1 (flat bunk, isolated) yields the longest FDP limit; Class 3 provides the least quality and the shortest augmented FDP limit.

q: How many consecutive nighttime FDPs infringing on the WOCL are Flight Crewmembers limited to, and what are the WOCL hours?
a: A maximum of three consecutive nighttime FDPs scheduled to infringe on the WOCL, which is 0200-0559.

src.quote: Flight Crewmembers are limited to a maximum of three consecutive nighttime FDPs that are scheduled to infringe on WOCL (0200-0559).
src.note: This applies whenever an FDP infringes on any part of the crewmember's Window of Circadian Low.

q: For a short-call reserve pilot, what is the maximum length of a Reserve Availability Period (RAP)?
a: The RAP may not exceed 14 hours.

src.quote: The Flight Crewmember’s RAP may not exceed 14 hours.
src.note: The combined RAP plus FDP may not exceed the lesser of the applicable Table B FDP limit plus 4 hours, or 16 hours, measured from the start of the RAP.

q: Within what time must a Fatigue Report be submitted for a fatigue call in order for pay protection to be considered?
a: Within 3 days of the fatigue event, in a timely manner.

src.quote: A Fatigue Report must be submitted for a fatigue call in a timely manner (within 3 days of the fatigue event) in order for pay protection to be considered.
src.note: If the FRP finds extenuating circumstances precluded timely submission, it may still accept the report for a pay evaluation.

q: By no later than what time prior to departure should the Captain be on board the aircraft?
a: On board prior to passenger boarding if possible, but no later than 25 minutes prior to departure.

src.quote: Captain – Be on board prior to passenger boarding, if possible, but no later than 25 minutes prior to departure.
src.note: The First Officer arrives at the aircraft at least 45 minutes prior for preflight and should be on board 20 minutes prior to departure.

q: PIC on a Pacific pairing, an unforeseen gate hold pushes you toward your FDP limit. What is the maximum FDP extension you may accept?
a: Up to 2 hours; no extension over 30 minutes for either pilot since their last 30 hours free from duty.

src.quote: Flight Duty Period (FDP) extensions of up to 2 hours are permitted provided: • Extension is required to address unforeseen operational circumstances. • Neither Flight Crewmember has experienced an extension greater than 30 minutes since the crewmember’s last period of 30 consecutive hours free from all duty.
src.note: Pilot Crew Scheduling and/or the Flight Operations Duty Officer are authorized to act on behalf of the certificate holder in agreeing upon the length of the extension.

q: After a red-eye crossing you are too fatigued to fly the next leg. What must you do to be removed from the assignment?
a: Contact and advise Pilot Crew Scheduling, and complete a Fatigue Report.

src.quote: If a Flight Crewmember feels they are too fatigued to fly, the Flight Crewmember shall contact and advise Pilot Crew Scheduling in order to be removed from the flight assignment. A Fatigue Report should be completed to identify and address any systemic conditions that caused the fatigue (see 7.2.2 – Reporting Program). (AS) Removal from assignments for flight time due to fatigue will not be cause for disciplinary action, and will be accomplished as follows:
src.note: To be considered for pay protection, the Fatigue Report must be submitted within 3 days of the event (FOM 4.3.1.4).

q: Before a RAP or between FDPs, what minimum rest period does Part 117 prescribe?
a: 10 consecutive hours from release from duty, including at least 8 uninterrupted hours of sleep opportunity.

src.quote: Part 117 prescribes the minimum rest period (prior to beginning a Reserve Availability Period (RAP) or between FDPs) as 10 consecutive hours measured from the time the Flight Crewmember is released from duty. This 10-hour rest period must provide the Flight Crewmember with a minimum of 8 uninterrupted hours of sleep opportunity.
src.note: The assignment must be scheduled in advance so the crewmember can plan to maximize sleep opportunity within the rest period.

q: Airborne, an unforeseen circumstance means finishing the flight will exceed your cumulative FDP limits. Is exceeding them permitted?
a: Yes. A post-takeoff FDP extension under 14 CFR 117.19 allows it, but expires once the aircraft lands.

src.quote: Under 14 CFR 117.19, a post-takeoff FDP extension allows a Flight Crewmember to exceed the cumulative FDP limits. However, a post-takeoff FDP extension is limited in that it expires once the aircraft lands. Once the flight on which the post-takeoff extension was used has been completed, the Flight Crewmember would again be bound by the cumulative FDP limitations.
src.note: Cumulative FDP limits are 60 hours in any 168 consecutive hours and 190 hours in any 672 consecutive hours.

q: Once a pre-takeoff FDP extension is agreed upon, how is its length confirmed and documented?
a: Via a recorded verbal communication or acknowledgment of an ACARS message specifying the length of the extension.

src.quote: Once an extension is agreed upon, the length of the extension will be confirmed and documented via a recorded verbal communication or acknowledgment of an ACARS message specifying the length of the extension.
src.note: Rev 125.3 deleted the HA-only Evidence of FDP Extension Concurrence process (the AOC OPS CTRL MSG "EXTEND FDP" message); this all-fleet method is what remains.
